name: llcpp
workload: Single-thread and 4-thread logging of lines to /tmp on SSD; per-call latency percentiles vs mini-async-logger, NanoLog, spdlog and g3log.
claimed_speedup: 1 thread: 165 ns median (timestamp) vs spdlog 729 ns (about 4.4x, derived from page data); 4 threads: 173 ns vs spdlog 1100 ns (about 6.4x, derived from page data). Total time 0.42 s vs 0.95 s (1 thread).
tradeoffs: Writes a binary log (format string plus raw argument bytes) that needs a separate script to turn into text; synchronous, no async backend; requires C++17 and a GNU user-defined string literal extension.
caveats: README marks it proof-of-concept; benchmarks from 2017 on old Clang with no CPU model stated; the benchmark harness is described in a blog post that is not reachable here (blapid.github.io blocked); spdlog was measured at default text formatting so the comparison is binary versus text output. Its own table shows spdlog with a better 99th percentile (973 ns vs 2058 ns, 1 thread).
found_via: Package registries search: 'github C++ logger faster than spdlog' led to llcpp blog part 3 benchmarks

workload: Google Benchmark of logging a 4-integer plus 128-byte-string record from 1-8 threads to file (scenario 1 saturated throughput, scenario 2 fixed iterations), nine C/C++ loggers compared.

hardware: Intel i7-10710U laptop (ThinkPad X1 Carbon 7th), CPU frequency pinned to 3.2GHz, Arch Linux, kernel 6.11.9
found_via: Package registries search: 'conan center C++ logger ultra low latency binary logging faster than spdlog' led to cc_log_benchmark
name: fmtlog
claimed_speedup: Named among the fastest libraries in both scenarios (with Nanolog, quill, haclog) versus spdlog, glog, loguru, easyloggingpp and reckless; results shown only as charts, no table of numbers on the page.
tradeoffs: Fastest mode drops logs when the buffer is full; blocking mode loses speed.
caveats: Independent single-machine laptop run; numbers are in SVG charts and report text files, not quoted here; flags not stated; not all scenarios covered for fmtlog, quill and reckless per the author.
